size 1000x600 with 1 Axes>","image/png":"\n"},"metadata":{}}],"execution_count":41},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"### Business Interpretation\nThe strongest common message from both models is that customer contract characteristics, internet-service characteristics, payment method, and tenure contain useful information for predicting churn.\nHowever, the models emphasize those variables differently:\n1. Random Forest spreads importance more broadly across financial, tenure, service, and contract variables.\n2. XGBoost concentrates importance heavily on contract and internet-service variables.\nWe should therefore report the agreement between the models rather than relying on only one model.\n**Important technical caution**\nWe should not interpret these importance scores as causal effects. For example, we cannot conclude that a two-year contract causes lower churn simply because XGBoost gives Contract_Two year high importance.\nAlso, because your dataset contains related variables such as tenure, MonthlyCharges, and TotalCharges, importance can be distributed differently between models when predictors contain overlapping information.\n#### Conclusion \nContract type, internet service characteristics, payment method, and customer tenure consistently emerge as important predictors across the tree-based models, although the relative importance assigned to individual features differs between Random Forest and XGBoost.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"#### Combined chart for XGBOOST and Random Forest feature importance.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"code","source":"# Prepare Random Forest feature importance\nrf_importance = pd.DataFrame({\n    'Feature': X_train.columns,\n    'Random Forest': random_forest_model.feature_importances_\n})\n\n# Prepare XGBoost feature importance\nxgb_importance = pd.DataFrame({\n    'Feature': X_train.columns,\n    'XGBoost': xgb_model.feature_importances_\n})\n\n# Merge both models\ncombined_importance = pd.merge(\n    rf_importance,\n    xgb_importance,\n    on='Feature'\n)\n\n# Calculate average importance\ncombined_importance['Average Importance'] = (\n    combined_importance['Random Forest'] +\n    combined_importance['XGBoost']\n) / 2\n\n# Select top 10 based on average importance\ntop_combined = combined_importance.sort_values(\n    by='Average Importance',\n    ascending=False\n).head(10)\n\ntop_combined\n\n\n# Reverse order for horizontal bar chart\nplot_data = top_combined.sort_values(\n    by='Average Importance',\n    ascending=True\n)\n\ny = np.arange(len(plot_data))\nheight = 0.35\n\nplt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))\n\nplt.barh(\n    y - height/2,\n    plot_data['Random Forest'],\n    height,\n    label='Random Forest'\n)\n\nplt.barh(\n    y + height/2,\n    plot_data['XGBoost'],\n    height,\n    label='XGBoost'\n)\n\nplt.yticks(y, plot_data['Feature'])\nplt.xlabel('Feature Importance')\nplt.ylabel('Feature')\nplt.title('Top 10 Feature Importance: Random Forest vs XGBoost')\nplt.legend()\n\nplt.tight_layout()\nplt.show()","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-08-22T15:11:28.135270Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-08-22T15:11:28.135625Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-08-22T15:11:28.418543Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-08-22T15:11:28.135587Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-08-22T15:11:28.417743Z"}},"outputs":[{"output_type":"display_data","data":{"text/plain":"<Figure Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost.\n\nThe models were compared using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Accuracy alone was not used to determine the best model because the target variable is moderately imbalanced, with churned customers representing approximately 26.54% of the dataset.\n\nLogistic Regression provides a simple and highly interpretable baseline, while Decision Tree can capture nonlinear relationships but may be susceptible to overfitting. Random Forest improves on a single decision tree by combining multiple trees, providing robust predictions and useful feature-importance information. XGBoost is a boosting-based ensemble method capable of learning complex relationships in structured customer data.\n\nThe final model will be selected based on the overall balance of predictive performance, particularly ROC-AUC, F1-score and Recall, together with interpretability and business suitability.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"code","source":"# The ranking table \nmodel_ranking = by considering ROC-AUC, F1-score, Recall, Precision, and Accuracy rather than relying on a single metric.\n\nFor this customer churn problem, Recall and F1-score are particularly important because the business needs to identify customers who are likely to churn while maintaining a reasonable level of precision.\n\nThe model with the strongest overall performance was selected as the final recommended model. Its performance provides the most suitable balance between correctly identifying potential churners and limiting incorrect predictions.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"### Final Model Recommendation\n\nBased on the evaluation results, XGBoost was selected as the preferred model for customer churn prediction.\n\nXGBoost achieved the highest ROC-AUC (0.8430), Recall (0.8102), and F1-score (0.6254) among the four models evaluated. Its high Recall indicates that it was able to identify a larger proportion of customers who actually churned.\n\nRandom Forest achieved the highest Accuracy (0.7821) and Precision (0.6184), but its Recall was considerably lower (0.4679). Since identifying potential churners is an important business objective, the ability to detect actual churners was given greater consideration than Accuracy alone.\n\nLogistic Regression performed competitively, with a ROC-AUC of 0.8417 and Recall of 0.7834, while Decision Tree produced the weakest overall performance, particularly in terms of ROC-AUC (0.6637).\n\nTherefore, XGBoost provides the best overall balance of discrimination, churn detection, and F1-score for this customer churn prediction problem.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"# Business Interpretation and Recommendations","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"The machine learning results provide useful insights into the factors associated with customer churn. XGBoost was selected as the preferred model because it achieved the highest ROC-AUC, Recall, and F1-score among the four evaluated models.\n\nThe feature-importance analysis from Random Forest and XGBoost indicates that contract type, internet service characteristics, payment method, tenure, and customer service-related variables contain important predictive information for churn.\n\nThese findings can be used to identify customers at higher risk of leaving and support targeted customer-retention strategies.\n\n### Key Business Findings\n\nThe feature-importance analysis from Random Forest and XGBoost identified several customer characteristics that provide important predictive information about churn.\n\nThe Random Forest model ranked TotalCharges, tenure, and MonthlyCharges as its three most important features. Contract type, internet service, payment method, and TotalServices were also among the important predictors.\n\nXGBoost placed particularly high importance on Contract_Two year, Contract_One year, InternetService_Fiber optic, and InternetService_No. PaymentMethod_Electronic check, StreamingMovies_Yes, tenure, OnlineSecurity_Yes, and PaperlessBilling_Yes were also among its top predictors.\n\nThe two models therefore show agreement on several broad areas, particularly contract type, internet service, payment method, and tenure, although the relative importance of individual features differs between the models.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"### Business Recommendations\n\nBased on the model results and feature-importance analysis, the following actions are recommended:\n\n1. **Focus on customers with higher churn risk**\n   Use the XGBoost model to identify customers who are likely to churn and prioritize them for retention campaigns.\n\n2. **Review contract strategies**\n   Since contract type is highly important in the XGBoost model, the company should investigate ways to encourage suitable customers to move from shorter-term contracts to longer-term contracts.\n\n3. **Monitor internet-service customers**\n   Internet service characteristics, particularly fiber-optic and the absence of internet service, were important predictors. The company should investigate service quality, pricing, and customer experience within these segments.\n\n4. **Improve retention of electronic-check customers**\n   Electronic check payment was an important predictor in both tree-based models. The company could investigate whether alternative payment options or payment-related customer experiences are associated with higher churn.\n\n5. **Pay attention to customer tenure and charges**\n   Tenure, MonthlyCharges, and TotalCharges were particularly important in the Random Forest model. Customers at different stages of their relationship and customers with higher charges should be monitored for potential churn risk.\n\n6. **Use targeted rather than broad retention campaigns**\n   Instead of offering incentives to every customer, the company can use predicted churn risk to prioritize customers who are most likely to leave.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"### Business Interpretation Limitation\n\nFeature importance indicates how useful a variable was to the model's predictions; it does not establish that the variable causes customer churn.\n\nTherefore, the identified predictors should be treated as signals for further business investigation rather than direct evidence of causal relationships.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"## Conclusion\n\nThis project developed and evaluated four classification models for predicting customer churn: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost.\n\nThe models were evaluated using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. XGBoost achieved the strongest overall performance, with a ROC-AUC of 0.8430, Recall of 0.8102, and F1-score of 0.6254. Although Random Forest achieved the highest Accuracy (0.7821) and Precision (0.6184), its Recall was substantially lower at 0.4679.\n\nFeature-importance analysis showed that different models relied on different predictors. Contract type, internet service characteristics, payment method, tenure, and customer charges were among the important predictors identified across the models.\n\nBased on the evaluation results, XGBoost was selected as the preferred model for this customer churn prediction problem because it provided the best overall balance between identifying customers who are likely to churn and maintaining predictive performance.\n\nThe model can support a telecom company's customer-retention strategy by helping identify customers at higher risk of churn and allowing retention efforts to be targeted more effectively.","metadata":{}}]}
